by: second master sommelier, the facts read after the researchers and the refuters
method: Every one of the 255 records was read in full for its facts (place, founding year, the wine's appellation, rank, grapes, sites, making, ageing, label, table line, story, others and traps), group by group against the review files, then across groups: every person named with dates was gathered into one list and each pair of dates compared and checked against what is known; serving temperatures were tabulated by colour against the Codex's service reference; repeated facts (the appellation and decree years, the Paris tasting, the Swartland Revolution, the Jordan division of 1848, the DAC years) were compared record against record and against the Codex's own data files.

Spot checks went to the strongest claims first: the deaths and dates of people of the last few years (a living person named as dead would break two rules at once), recent ownership changes, claims of a first or an only, classification and decree years, and the facts a refuter had left open.
A search summary drawn from a body's or a house's own domain is read as that body; the sources of every check are listed with it. No WebFetch was tried.
Fragments were changed only where a check showed a fact wrong or unsettled; each change was linted sound with build-flagships.cjs --lint, and the writing build was never run.
